D3b closing (second batch). Every re-check line is ruled: 53,493 of 53,493 (validate.py D3: 95,736 of 95,736 ledger lines ruled, 0 errors, 2 old warnings). This batch wrote 18,698 rulings: the 18,674 new lines once each, 20 earlier lines re-ruled and 4 second-batch lines re-ruled inside the batch, each by a logged reading and a re-rule file. The 323 propose lines: 267 particulars, 54 rejected, 2 accepted as a pair (paladins, portugal), held. The 161 re-check verdict splits are ruled under G62: 160 composes, 1 with residue (TheHulk); the room verdicts after are 630 composes, 56 with residue, 19 cannot tell, 0 does not compose. The rewrite fixed what its evidence pointed at: R01 in 11 of 12 rooms (hearthstone a repeat whose condition R01 now holds), P05 in its 4 cause rooms, A21 in 34 of 36 (two repeats); P21, P22 and moves 177 to 181 draw no correction. Held, no move: P05's added clause fails in 6 rooms where keepers read the plan from its shape (two pairs at one node, section 2 met twice, the alignment holding; a relating revision proposed; QD3-011 asks J whether to make it now with a second re-check before the freeze); R01's 4 corrections, no trigger, move dropped, wording to D3c; the pair beside P34. notes-D3.md has the second-batch section, the 705-row table v4 and the close-check; the head is 2,999 words. Working hypothesis: the revised model composes nearly every room once its candidates hold the chats, explaining, arrivals and jokes, and its one live failure is P05's telling clause. Next: QD3-011's answer, then D3c.

D3c opened. Oriented: AGENT.md, the head (2,999 words), the stage file, the last five diary entries, validate.py --open D3 (its one error is the expected EXPECTATIONS.jsonl, which I do not read). Answers read: QD3-009 and QD3-010 (both already taken up at D3b) and QD3-011 (J, 23 Oct 10:36 Berlin): option (b). Hold the P05 move; freeze 46384686 at D3c; report P05's added clause as failing in completeanarchy, polska, satania, halo, bangtan and thesilphroad; name armok, maryland and oneshot, where informed members carry the change; carry the drafted revision to D4 as a held proposal with its rooms and lines; keep R01; hold the paladins and portugal proposal beside P34; and state in notes-D3.md how (b) meets the stage's line 'An exception cannot be printed beside an unchanged universal claim as a substitute for a scope decision', or ask if it cannot. Work that rested on my QD3-011 assumption (no move, held proposals in the notes, D3b closed) agrees with (b) and stands. Facts checked first: vlib.model_hash covers model/elements.jsonl, arrows, loops, fourth, dimensions, scheme_v2 and assignments_final (now 46384686...); findings.jsonl, history.jsonl and account.md are outside it; P05 has no scope or bound field, so its clause's scope lives only in its statement; no finding touches P05. Plan: write the scope decision's rule before acting on it, then the blind re-rule check, the exception report, the re-lift, the re-read against the amendments, the counts read last, the handback, the interview brief and the head, and close with done.sh D3 --cut interview.

The scope decision for P05's added clause under QD3-011's option (b), logged before any write that rests on it (rule 12; stage section 4; QD3-007's precedent of a subform carried for the clustering). The clause, frozen in P05's statement at 46384686, reads: 'A change the room has planned or agreed (P02) is therefore repaired away as damage until its keepers are told of it, and it is lost or given up where the telling does not reach them.' It fails as stated in 9 rooms. (1) The decision is a cluster branch with a bound, not a global revision at D3. Stage section 4 allows it ('Repeated corrections can define a cluster branch; they do not force the same revision everywhere'), and rule 12 names the cluster branch beside global revision as what the comparison and its written reason warrant. (2) The trunk is the frozen clause, bounded: it holds where the keepers can learn of a planned change only by being told and no informed member holds it. (3) The branch, 'the shape read': completeanarchy, polska, satania, halo, bangtan and thesilphroad, where keepers stop repairing the change once its shape shows what it is, with no telling. Its warrant is D3b's re-examination, with two pairs meeting at one node (polska and satania at T4-006, halo and bangtan at T4-019). It is carried to D4 and D5, where cluster branches are built and their adequacy is judged. (4) armok, maryland and oneshot, where informed members hold the change against keepers who do not know, are paired corrections at three nodes, below the trigger. They are named in the bound as a second limit of the trunk, not as a branch. (5) The global revision drafted at D3b is held for D4 with its rooms and lines (QD3-011). (6) The record: a new finding, F-024, states the bounded claim with its bound, refuted_by and status 'bounded' (rule 14), since no finding touched P05; notes-D3.md states the decision and how it meets the line; exception-report-D.md lists the 9 rooms under P05; handback-D3.md carries it. None of these files is in the model hash. (7) What stays: P05's words in elements.jsonl are unchanged, because the re-check was served on them (section 5). Read alone, the sentence is still universal in form, and D4 must read it with F-024. If J reads the line as requiring the element's own words to carry the scope, then (b) cannot meet it without a model change and a second re-check. The notes say so.

F-024 written (findings.jsonl 38 lines, wc -l; by out/_analysis/d3c_finding_f024.py, which first checked that the 9 cited re-check lines sit on P05 with an accepted correction as their last ruling and that the 11 cited concepts exist; the halo quote was read through cite.py). It states P05's added clause as a bounded claim: the told route holds where keepers can learn of a planned change only by being told and no informed member holds it; the shape-read branch (completeanarchy, polska, satania, halo, bangtan, thesilphroad) is carried to D4 and D5; armok, maryland and oneshot are named as a second limit; status bounded; two refuted_by conditions. mem.py findings --touching P05 now returns F-024. The model hash is untouched (findings.jsonl is not a model file).

The rules of the blind re-rule check before the D3c freeze (J, 16 October, 19:08 Berlin: about 50 lines, pairs left for the handler's kappa), logged before the draw. (1) 50 lines: 46 drawn and 4 forced. The forced lines are the four the first-batch notes named for this check (anaheimducks-066, hatsune-025, neu-057, slovenia-029). They are flagged 'forced' in the sample and reported apart, since their history is written in the notes. (2) The draw, seed 2026102310, by a new script (out/_analysis/d3c_blind_sample.py). Population A is first-return lines whose last ruling was written at D3a-10 to D3a-54, the groups ruled after the first check: 20 lines, by op (instantiate 8, restrict 4, add-condition 3, add-step 2, link 2, absent 1). Population B is re-check lines whose last ruling is a D3b reading and not a G61 (1) repeat, written before 2026-10-23T06:20Z, so that nothing ruled in my present working context is drawn: 26 lines, by op (instantiate 9, restrict 6, add-condition 4, add-step 3, link 3, absent 1). Both exclude propose lines and NONPORTABLE lines (particulars by construction). (3) Blindness: the lines are read through a new packet script (d3c_blind_packet.py) that prints every field and the element's statement and range, and no decision, kind, pair or reason of mine. The G rules may be read; the notes' rulings of these lines are not. Quotes come through cite.py. (4) The blind rulings are written to out/_analysis/d3c_blind/blind-rulings-D3c.jsonl before any comparison. The pairs are written by d3c_blind_pairs.py with both rulings and reasons, raw agreement is reported, and the kappa is the handler's. (5) The check changes no ruling unless it finds an error (rule 13), which would be fixed by an appended re-ruling with its reason.
